# Preferences Template

```yaml
# Superpowers Workflow Preferences
# Auto-generated by the onboarding wizard.
# Edit manually or ask the agent to update.

# qa_gate: the end-of-implementation QA gate (super.user-story-verification — e.g. headless-browser
#   Playwright E2E driven by QA subagents from the PRD), only when a PRD exists. true (default) runs
#   it automatically — nothing is asked at the final stage. ask asks once at the gate, per feature.
#   false disables it silently (QA never runs and is never mentioned, even at the PRD step).
# visual_companion: offer the browser companion (mockups/diagrams) during super.brainstorming.
#   true (default) keeps the consent question before anything opens; false skips the companion
#   entirely — never offered, never mentioned.
# finish_action: what super.finishing-a-development-branch does once the branch is verified.
#   ask (default) shows the finishing menu; merge merges locally; pr pushes and opens a pull
#   request; keep leaves the branch as-is. Discard is never automatic.
workflow:
  auto_commit: <true|false>
  qa_gate: <true|ask|false>
  visual_companion: <true|false>
  finish_action: <ask|merge|pr|keep>

# Platform-specific settings.
# The `copilot:` section is silently ignored by Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI.
# review_final: run the native `review` skill at the final review as an extra bug-focused pass on top
#   of the default final reviewer. Additive (spec + quality gates always run); no effort levels.
copilot:
  review_final: false

# Platform-specific settings.
# The `claude_code:` section is silently ignored by Copilot CLI, Codex, and Gemini CLI.
# Off by default — the user opts in during onboarding (Claude Code only).
# This native skill is ADDITIVE: the spec review and quality review gates always run.
# review_final: run /code-review at the final review as an extra bug-focused pass on top
#   of the default final reviewer.
# review_effort: low | medium | high | max (ultra unsupported — cloud, separate tier).
claude_code:
  review_final: false
  review_effort: medium

# Context settings. Optional — added during onboarding if the user provides corporate artifacts.
# When has_corporate_artifacts is true, the agent reads .superpowers/corporate-artifacts.yml
# for local paths and public URLs to corporate documents (PRDs, specs, UML diagrams, wikis, etc.)
context:
  has_corporate_artifacts: false

# Model tier → concrete model mapping for THIS harness (optional).
# Execution skills choose an abstract tier per task (see super.subagent-driven-development,
# "Model Selection" section); this maps each tier to a real model name. Leave a value empty to let
# the harness pick its own cheap/standard/capable model ("auto").
# Names are per-harness: a tier naming a model the harness you are running does not serve is
# treated as empty (auto) for that session, and the session summary says which one it dropped.
model_tiers:
  cheap:
  standard:
  capable:

# Project profile — what THIS repo is: the ecosystem label and the manifest that describes it.
# Proposed by detect-project.cjs during onboarding and confirmed by the user. Commands (test,
# setup, format) are NOT preferences: the repo's instructions file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) and the
# manifest carry them, and the agent reads those when it needs one. Leave both empty when the
# stack is not decided yet.
project:
  stack: <node|flutter|python|rust|go|...>
  manifest: <repo-relative path, e.g. "package.json" / "pubspec.yaml" / "pyproject.toml">
```
